subject: Post-demo cost follow-up: tokens vs characters vs requests (summary + next steps)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Soto <carmen.soto@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-02T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up & concise pricing summary from today’s demo

Hi Carmen —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the two items you asked for on the call:

1) Short, plain-language clarification on the different billing units we discussed (tokens vs characters vs requests).
2) A worked example for your projected workload so you can map to your $/1M token target and the months where caching affects billed units.

Below is a compact table and a small example — I’ll follow up with a spreadsheet if you want to run alternate volume assumptions. If this looks right, next step is a short PO/term sheet and then procurement finalization.

---
Tokens vs characters vs requests (short):
- Tokens: what we bill. Tokens are chunks of text our models consume/generate. A single request may consume many tokens depending on prompt + response length.
- Characters: a rough proxy for prompt size but not used for billing. Useful for estimating token counts if you know average characters per token (English =~4 chars/token, but varies).
- Requests: API calls. We do not bill per-request by default for text generation; billing is per-token. Requests matter for concurrency/throughput SLOs.

Prompt caching vs billed tokens:
- Cached prompts (exact same prompt + model + model-version + temperature) can drastically reduce billed tokens for repeated identical calls.
- We still bill response tokens when a response is generated, but if we short-circuit and return a cached response, billed tokens are reduced to a small cache-key overhead.

Worked example (your numbers from the call):
- Monthly active users: 120k
- Average requests per user / month: 3
- Avg prompt length: 600 characters (~150 tokens)
- Avg response length: 350 characters (~88 tokens)
- Total requests/month: 360k
- Estimated tokens/request (prompt + response): ~238 tokens
- Estimated tokens/month: 85,680,000 (~86M)

Unit pricing examples (illustrative):
- At $10 / 1M tokens => $860 / month
- At $5 / 1M tokens => $430 / month

If prompt caching hits for 25% of requests with full cache hits (returns cached response): billed tokens drop to ~64.5M => cost at $10/1M = $645.

Next steps:
- I’ll attach a one-page SOW (draft) and a simple volume sheet for you to tweak.
- Please confirm if the 4 chars/token assumption is OK for your content (most customers with English UI text see 3.5–4.5).

Thanks —
Soojín Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Great questions — answers below and I’ve looped Rishi for the infra/caching nuance.

1) Cache scope and model pinning:
- Our prompt/response cache is keyed by model identifier + model version + prompt + certain routing parameters (temperature, top_p). If you want cache continuity across minor model updates we recommend pinning the model version for that route; otherwise a new model version will miss the cache. We can set automatic fallback policies for rollouts to reduce cold-cache impact.

2) JSON metadata in prompts:
- JSON objects increase token counts roughly proportional to their length; because punctuation and short keys can be token-dense, the simple chars/token rule drifts down (i.e., fewer chars per token). For prompts containing structured JSON we recommend measuring a sample (we can provide a small script) — but plan conservatively: assume 3 chars/token if payloads are heavy with punctuation.

Attached: draft SOW + a one-tab CSV with the numbers from my email so your procurement team can adjust assumptions quickly.

If helpful, Rishi can propose a conservative caching uplift % for the first 3 months to help with budgeting (we see 10–35% depending on UX patterns).

Regards,
Soojín

Hi Carmen — quick add from infra side:

- Caching behavior we observe: identical prompt + model_version => cache hit ~95% when the UX returns identical input. If your UI appends changing timestamps/session ids the hit rate collapses. We typically recommend canonicalizing any volatile fields (e.g., session ids) on the client side before sending to maximize caching.

- Billing note: we bill based on tokens consumed by the request path that actually executes. So if the request hits a cached response and we return that body without re-running the model, billed tokens are minimal (cache-key overhead + stored response size). If we re-run because of model mismatch, we bill full tokens.

- For budgeting guidance: if you want to target $800 / month at your expected volumes (~86M tokens), that implies ~ $9.3 / 1M tokens effective. If you can guarantee a 20% cache-hit rate in steady-state the gross $/1M can be higher because billed tokens shrink.

Happy to run a scenario sheet with three glidepaths (0%, 20%, 40% cache) if you want numbers for procurement.

-rishi
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
